qs.q: In pteridophytes, to prevent self-fertilisation_
o: There is high degree of sterility
Antherozoids and eggs mature at different times
qs.s: Pteridophytes exhibit dichogamy, the maturation of male and female sex organs at different times to prevent self fertilisation.

qs.q: Heterosporous pteridophytes are
qs.s: Genera Selaginella and Salvinia are heterosporous pteridophytes.

qs.q: Pick out the statement that does not apply to bryophytes:
o: The gametophyte is not differentiated into root, stem and leaf - like structures
The gametophyte bears root - like structures called rhizoids
The gametophyte bears muiticellular sex organs like antheridium and archegonium
qs.s: In Bryophytes, the gametophyte is thalloid or differentiated into root-like, stem-like and leaf-like structures.

qs.q: Angiosperms are also called
qs.s: In the angiosperms, the pollen grains and ovules are developed in specialised structures called flowers. Hence, they are also known as flowering plants.

qs.q: Syngamy can occur outside the body of the organism in
qs.s: Syngamy is the process of fusion of male and female gametes to form zygote, and external fusion called syngamy occurs in a majority of algae.

qs.q: The first seeded plants are the
qs.s: Gymnosperms were the first seed bearing plants in the process of evolution. Sequoia is one of the tallest gymnosperms.

qs.q: Zygote of bryophyte
o: Undergoes reduction division just after formation
qs.s: Zygotes in bryophytes do not undergo reduction division immediately. They produce a multicellular body called a sporophyte.

qs.q: Which of the following plant lacks true roots, stem and leaves?
qs.s: True roots, stem and leaves having vascular supply are absent in bryophytes, but root-like, non-vascular rhizoids and leaf-like and stem-like structures are present.

qs.q:
Match the columns I and II.
A. Double fertilization - S. Angiosperms
B. Zygote - R. Embryo
C. Ovule - P. Seed
D. Ovary - T. Fruit
E. Female sex organ - Q. Archegonia
qs.s: Matching correct pairs gives A-S, B-R, C-P, D-T, E-Q according to standard plant organ transformations.

qs.q: In gymnosperms, two kinds of spores are produced within sporangia that are borne on sporophylls which
o: Are arranged spirally along an axis to form compact strobili or cones only.
Are arranged spirally along an axis to form lax strobili or cones only.
Are arranged in a linear manner along an axis to form lax or compact strobili or cones.
Are arranged spirally along an axis to form lax or compact strobili or cones.
qs.s: The two kinds of heterospores are produced within sporangia that are borne on sporophylls which are arranged spirally along an axis to form lax or compact strobili or cones.

qs.q:
Which statement is correct for homosporous pteridophytes?
(I) Gametophyte and sporophyte are usually parasitic.
(II) Gametophyte is autotrophic, while the sporophyte is parasitic.
(III) Gametophyte is a parasite, and the sporophyte is autotrophic.
(IV) Sporophyte is autotrophic.
Options:
(1) I
(2) II
(3) III
(4) IV
qs.s: Sporophyte is autotrophic in case of homosporous pteridophyta.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding gymnosperms and choose the incorrect option
(1) In gymnosperms endosperm is formed before fertilisation.
(2) The multicellular female gametophyte is retained within megasporangium
(3) The gymnosperms are heterosporous.
(4) In gymnosperms, the male and female gametophytes have an independent existence
qs.s: In gymnosperms, male and female gametophyte are both dependent on sporophyte and lack an independent free-living existence.

qs.q: Carrageen is a
qs.s: Carrageen is a hydrocolloid obtained from red algae.

qs.q:
A) Phylogenetic system of classification is based upon evolutionary relationship of organisms
B) Phylogenetic classification systems are based on numbers and codes are assigned to it
C) Cytotaxonomy is based on cytological information like chromosome number, structure and behaviour.
qs.s: Numerical taxonomy is based on numbers and codes, whereas A and C correctly describe phylogenetic classification and cytotaxonomy.

qs.q: The cones having megasporophylls with ovules are called:
qs.s: The cones having megasporophylls with ovules are called female cones or female strobili or megasporangiate strobili.

qs.q: Phaeophyceae vary in colour from various shades of ___ to ___ depending on the amount of pigment ___ and ___ present in them
qs.s: Brown algae vary in colour from olive green to various shades of brown depending upon the amount of the xanthophyll pigment, fucoxanthin.

qs.q: In which of the following groups do the male and female gametophytes have independent, free living existence?
qs.s: Unlike gymnosperms, bryophytes and pteridophytes have independent free-living gametophytes.

qs.q: In angiosperms, seeds are enclosed by
qs.s: In angiosperms, the seeds are enclosed in fruits.

qs.q: Vascular plants, with seeds but no fruits are
qs.s: Gymnosperms are vascular plants with naked seeds, lacking fruits.

qs.q: The spores and gametes of red algae are
qs.s: Spores and gametes in red algae are both non-motile due to the absence of flagella.

qs.q: Female sex organ of the bryophyte is called
qs.s: The female sex organ in bryophytes is called archegonium, which is flask-shaped and produces a single egg.

qs.q: Fern plant in its dominant phase is a
qs.s: The zygote produces a multicellular well-differentiated sporophyte which is the dominant phase of pteridophytes/ferns.

qs.q: The cell wall of the vegetative cells of phaeophyceae are made up of
qs.s: The vegetative cells of phaeophyceae have a cellulosic wall covered on the outside by a gelatinous coating of algin.

qs.q: The female sex organ of flowering plant is called
qs.s: The female sex organ in a flower is the carpel or pistil.

qs.q: Ovary is the characteristic of which of the followwing division
qs.s: In angiosperms, ovules are enclosed inside an ovary, which is a characteristic feature.

qs.q:
Which of the following statement is incorrect with respect to bryophytes?
(1) The plant body is thallus like, more differentiated than algae and attached to substratum by the help of holdfast.
(2) Bryophytes mostly occur in humid, damp and shaded localities
(3) Zygote formed undergoes mitosis immediately
(4) They have leaf like, stem like and root like structures.
qs.s: Bryophytes attach to the substratum by rhizoids, not holdfast.

qs.q: Fusion of two motile gametes which are dissimilar in size is termed as
qs.s: Fusion of gametes that are dissimilar in size is known as anisogamy.

qs.q: Bryophytes resemble algae in the following aspects:
o: Differentiation of plant body into root, stem and leaves and autotrophic nutrition
Thallus like plant body, presence of roots and autotrophic nutrition
Thallus like plant body, lack of vascular tissues and auto trophic nutrition
Filamentous body, presence of vascular tissues and auto-trophic nutrition
qs.s: Both lack vascular tissues and have a thallus-like plant body with autotrophic nutrition.

qs.q:
Read the following statements carefully
Mosses and ferns are found in moist and shady places because
(a) They get killed by sunlight
(b) They are dependent on water for asexual reproduction
(c) They are dependent on bacteria for their nutrition which survive only in shades
(d) They are dependent on water for fertilisation.
Select the incorrect statements.
(1) a, b, d
(2) a, b, c
(3) b, c, d
(4) a, c, d
qs.s: Mosses and ferns are found in moist places because they are dependent on water for fertilization; statements a, b, and c are incorrect.

qs.q: The diploid sporophyte is dominant in life cycle of
qs.s: Eucalyptus and Sunflower are both angiosperms, in which the sporophyte is the dominant plant body.

qs.q: Sexual reproduction is of isogamous, anisogamous and oogamous in
qs.s: Chlorophyceae and Phaeophyceae show isogamous, anisogamous, and oogamous sexual reproduction.

qs.q: Which one is/are correct about heterosporous pteridophytes?
o: The female gametophytes are retained on the parent sporophyte for variable period
Microspore and megaspores develop into the male and female gametophytes respectively
The development of the zygote into the embryo takes place within female gametophyte
qs.s: All given statements are correct features of heterosporous pteridophytes.

qs.q: Haplo-diplontic life cycle is seen in
qs.s: Both bryophytes and pteridophytes exhibit a haplo-diplontic life cycle.

qs.q: If the diploid number of a flowering plant is 36. What would be the chromosome number in its endosperm
qs.s: Endosperm in angiosperms is triploid (3n). If 2n = 36, then n = 18, so 3n = 54.

qs.q: Which of the following statements is true?
o: Trimerous condition of floral whorls is characterstic of dicotyledons
Adiantum is also called flying fern
In gymnosperms the vascular system consists of xylem without vessels and phloem with companion cells
qs.s: Riccia and Marchantia are well-known liverworts belonging to bryophytes.

qs.q: In gymnosperms, the pollen chamber represents
o: A cavity in the ovule in which pollen grains are stored after pollination
An opening in the mega gametophyte through which the pollen approaches the egg
The megasporangium in which pollengrains develop
A cell in the pollen grain in which the sperms are formed.
qs.s: The pollen chamber is a cavity in the ovule in which pollen grains are stored after pollination.

qs.q:
In which of the following distinct, independent gametophytic and sporophytic generations are found in their life cycle?
A. Adiantum B. Psilotum C. Selaginella
qs.s: Adiantum, Psilotum, and Selaginella are all pteridophytes with distinct, independent gametophytic and sporophytic generations.

qs.q: Most of the red algae
qs.s: Most of the red algae are multicellular with complex body organization.

qs.q: Plants of this group are diploid and well adapted to extreme conditions. They grow bearing sporophylls in compact structures called cones. The group in reference is
qs.s: Gymnosperms bear sporophylls in compact structures called cones and are adapted to extreme conditions.

qs.q: Spore in bryophytes are formed
qs.s: Some cells of the sporophyte capsule undergo reduction division to form haploid spores.

qs.q: The main plant body of pteridophytes is
qs.s: In pteridophytes, the main plant body is a sporophyte differentiated into true root, stem, and leaves.

qs.q: In flowering plants, meiosis occurs at the time of
qs.s: Meiosis occurs during microspore and megaspore mother cell division for pollen and female spore formation.

qs.q:
Identify the correct sequence of various developmental stages in the life cycle of bryophytes:
Options:
(1) Gametophyte → Gametes → Foot, Seta, Capsule → Spores → Sporophyte.
(2) Gametophyte → Foot, Seta, Capsule → Sporophyte → Gametes → Spores.
(3) Spores → Sporophyte → Foot, Seta, Capsule → Gametophyte → Gametes.
(4) Foot, Seta, Capsule → Sporophyte → Gametophyte → Spores → Gametes.
qs.s: Spores germinate into gametophytes, producing gametes that form the sporophyte (foot, seta, capsule). [Figure omitted]

qs.q: In Rhodophyceae reserve food is
qs.s: Reserve food in red algae is floridean starch, which is structurally very similar to amylopectin and glycogen.

qs.q: The precursor to the seed habit is found in_ [Figure omitted]
qs.s: Heterosporous pteridophytes like Selaginella show the precursor to seed habit. [Figure omitted]

qs.q: Pollen grains is
qs.s: Pollen grains represent highly reduced male gametophytes.

qs.q:
Which of the following is correctly matched?
(I) Chlorophyceae: Chlorophyll a + b + pecto-cellulosic cell wall.
(II) Phaeophyceae: Chlorophyll a + c + carrageen in the cell wall.
(III) Diatoms: Chlorophyll a + c + CaCO3 cell wall.
(IV) Rhodophyceae: Chlorophyll a + b + phycoerythrin.
Options:
(1) I
(2) II
(3) III
(4) IV
qs.s: Statement I correctly matches Chlorophyceae pigments and pecto-cellulosic cell wall.

qs.q: Cyanobacteria are classified under
qs.s: Cyanobacteria are prokaryotes and are classified under Kingdom Monera.

qs.q:
Which of the statements given below are correct about protonema?
(1) Adult stage of moss is protonema
(2) It consists of slender, green, branching system of filaments
(3) Develops directly from a zygote
(4) All of the above
qs.s: The protonema stage consists of a creeping, green, branched, and frequently filamentous system of filaments.

qs.q: Vegetative reproduction in mosses takes place by
o: Fragmentation and budding in secondary protonema
Fragmentation and gemma in secondary protonema
Fragmentation and budding in primary protonema
Fragmentation and gemma in primary protonema
qs.s: Vegetative reproduction in mosses is by fragmentation and budding in the secondary protonema.

qs.q: In gymnosperms, the endosperm is
qs.s: In gymnosperms, a haploid endosperm is formed before fertilisation and is equivalent to the female gametophyte.

qs.q: Isogamy is seen in
qs.s: Isogamous gametes are seen in both Ulothrix and Spirogyra.

qs.q:
Match the columns I and II.
A. Leaf-like appendages in two rows - Q. Marchantia
B. Slender axes bearing spirally arranged leaf-like appendages - R. Sphagnum
C. Presence of true leaves - P. Equisetum
qs.s: Correct matching is A-Q, B-R, C-P based on plant morphological characteristics.

qs.q: Moss peat is used as a packing material for sending flowers and live plants to distant places because-
qs.s: Sphagnum peat has a high water-holding capacity (hygroscopic) making it ideal for packing live plants.

qs.q: The complex post-fertilization events are seen in
qs.s: Gracilaria and Porphyra are red algae that show complex post-fertilisation events.

qs.q: The plants frequently grown as ornamentals and are used for medicinal purpose belong to
qs.s: Pteridophytes are frequently grown as ornamentals and used for medicinal purposes as well as soil-binders.

qs.q: Peat used in transshipment is a product obtained from
qs.s: Peat is obtained from Sphagnum, which is a moss.

qs.q: Ectocarpus, Dictyota, Laminaria, Sargassum and Fucus belongs to
qs.s: These genera belong to Phaeophyceae, commonly known as brown algae.

qs.q:
Identify the correct answer.
i. The most common spores in algae
ii. They are flagellated (motile) and on germination gives rise to new plants.
qs.s: Zoospores are the most common flagellated, motile spores in algae.

qs.q: Bryophytes reproduce by
qs.s: Bryophytes show vegetative, asexual, and sexual modes of reproduction.

qs.q: Gemmae are present in:
qs.s: Most liverworts reproduce asexually by means of gemmae held in gemma cups.

qs.q: The giant redwood tree (Sequoia sempervirens) is a/an
qs.s: Sequoia is a tall gymnosperm known as the giant redwood tree.

qs.q:
Match the words of Column I with that of Column II and choose the correct answer given below.
A. Algae - R. Autotrophic
B. Riccia - S. Livewort
C. Spirogyra - Q. Pond scum
D. Gnetum - P. Gymnosperm
qs.s: Matching pairs correctly associates Algae with autotrophic, Riccia with liverwort, Spirogyra with pond scum, and Gnetum with gymnosperm.

qs.q:
Choose the incorrect statements for Gymnosperms:
(I) Pollination in gymnosperms is mainly carried by air currents.
(II) The multicellular female gametophyte of gymnosperms is retained within the megasporangium.
(III) They are heterosporous.
(IV) Ovules are enclosed by an ovary wall.
(V) All gymnosperms are dioecious without any exception.
Options:
(1) I, II, V
(2) I, III, IV, V
(3) IV, V
(4) I, IV
qs.s: Statements IV and V are incorrect because ovules are naked (not enclosed in an ovary wall) and gymnosperms can be monoecious or dioecious.

qs.q: Gymnosperms bear seeds but lack fruits because they lack
qs.s: Gymnosperms lack an ovary, which is why their seeds remain naked and do not develop into fruits.

qs.q: Isogamous condition with non-flagellated gametes is found in
qs.s: Spirogyra produces non-flagellated, isogamous gametes.

qs.q: In Selaginella the embryo develops into
qs.s: The zygote in Selaginella develops into an embryo and further into a well-differentiated sporophyte.

qs.q: Natural classification system developed were based on
qs.s: Natural classification systems considered natural affinities and external/internal features like anatomy, embryology, and phytochemistry.

qs.q: Laminarion and mannitol are compounds found in
qs.s: Laminarin and mannitol are stored food reserves in brown algae such as Fucus.

qs.q:
Some examples of plants are given here, which of the following have predominantly sporophytic plant bodies?
Eucalyptus, Rose, Wheat, Euglena, Ulothrix, Cycas, Spirogyra, Polytrichum, Lycopodium, Pinus, Volvox, Funaria.
o: Eucalyptus, Rose, Wheat, Lycopodium, Pinus, Cycas
qs.s: Eucalyptus, Rose, Wheat, Lycopodium, Pinus, and Cycas all have a predominant sporophytic plant body.

qs.q: Egg apparatus of angiosperms contain
qs.s: The egg apparatus of angiosperms contains one egg cell and two synergids.

qs.q: Pyriform gametes means
qs.s: Pyriform gametes refer to pear-shaped gametes.

qs.q: In gymnosperms, the male and female gametophyte
o: May be born on same or different tree.
Remain within the sporangia retained on parent sporophyte.
Do not have independent free living existence
qs.s: All statements correctly describe gymnosperm gametophytes.

qs.q: The characters used to classify organism when no fossil evidence is supportive is
qs.s: Numerical taxonomy, chemotaxonomy, and cytotaxonomy are used when fossil evidence is lacking.

qs.q: Secondary protonema
o: Formed by other vegetative part of leafy stage
qs.s: Secondary protonema develops from vegetative parts (like a lateral bud) and gives rise to the leafy gametophyte.

qs.q: The sex organ in bryophytes are
qs.s: The sex organs in bryophytes are multicellular (antheridium and archegonium).

qs.q:
Pteridophytes are
I. Homosporous and produce only one kind of spores.
II. Zygote produces a multicellular well differentiated sporophyte
III. Heterosporus and produce small and large spores.
IV. Restricted to narrow geographical zone because of specific requirement of water.
qs.s: Pteridophytes can be homosporous or heterosporous, produce a multicellular sporophyte, and need water for fertilization, restricting their spread.

qs.q: Conifers are adapted to tolerate extreme environmental conditions because of
qs.s: Needle-like leaves, thick cuticles, and sunken stomata help conifers tolerate extreme conditions.

qs.q:
How many of the following algae belong to the category of red algae?
Spirogyra, Gelidium, Laminaria, Polysiphonia, Porphyra, Fucus, Gracilaria
qs.s: Gelidium, Polysiphonia, Porphyra, and Gracilaria are red algae (total 4).

qs.q: If you are asked to classify the various algae into distinct groups, which of the following characters you should choose?
o: Nature of food materials in the cell
Chemical composition of the cell wall
Types of pigments present in cell wall
qs.s: The presence of different types of major photosynthetic pigments forms the primary basis of classification in algae.

qs.q: Agar-agar is obtained from
qs.s: Agar-agar is commercially obtained from the red algae Gelidium and Gracilaria.

qs.q: Which one of the following plants is monoecious?
qs.s: Pinus is a monoecious gymnosperm bearing both male and female cones on the same plant.

qs.q: Which of the following can be called as amphibians of the plant_
qs.s: Bryophytes are called amphibians of the plant kingdom because they live in soil but depend on water for sexual reproduction.

qs.q: The bryophyte have an aquatic ancestry. Which of the following best explains this?
qs.s: The presence of flagellated sperms requiring water to swim to the egg highlights their aquatic ancestry.

qs.q: Sporophytic, generation is dominant phase in the life cycle of
qs.s: The sporophytic generation is dominant in all pteridophytes, including Selaginella, Equisetum, and Salvinia.

qs.q: Which of the following groups of marine algae is used as food?
qs.s: Many species of Porphyra, Laminaria, and Sargassum are used as marine food algae.

qs.q: Ovules are not enclosed by the ovaries in
qs.s: In gymnosperms, ovules are exposed and not enclosed by any ovary wall.

qs.q: Agar is commercially obtained from
qs.s: Gelidium and Gracilaria are red algae from which agar is commercially obtained.

qs.q: The structure of the plant body of a pteridophyte
o: Is the most well-developed in plant kingdom
Posses true root, leaves and stem
qs.s: Pteridophytes are the first terrestrial plants to possess true roots, stems, and leaves.

qs.q: Pteridophytes are called vascular cryptogams, because they are non-seeded plants containing:
qs.s: Pteridophytes have vascular tissues (xylem and phloem) but do not produce seeds.

qs.q: Gametophyte of pteridophyte
qs.s: The gametophyte in pteridophytes is small, inconspicuous, but multicellular and photosynthetic (prothallus).

qs.q: The female gametophytes are retained on the parent sporophyte in
o: They are never retained on sporophyte
Homosporous and Heterosporous species of pteridophytes
qs.s: In heterosporous pteridophytes, the female gametophytes are retained on the parent sporophytes.

qs.q: Stamen consists of
qs.s: Each stamen consists of a slender filament with an anther at the tip.

qs.q: In mosses the sex organs are present
o: At the mid-point of the leafy shoots
At the apex of the leafy shoots
At the base of the leafy shoots
qs.s: In mosses, sex organs are produced at the apex of the leafy shoots.

qs.q:
Match the columns I and II
A. Cycas - Q. Dioecious
B. Pinus - P. Monoecious
C. Sequoia - R. The giant red wood tree
qs.s: Correct match is A-Q, B-P, C-R linking Cycas to dioecious, Pinus to monoecious, and Sequoia to the giant redwood tree.

qs.q: Pollen grains are released from
qs.s: Pollen grains (microspores) are released from the microsporangia.

qs.q: Identify the pair of heterosporous pteridophytes among the following:
qs.s: Selaginella and Salvinia are well-known heterosporous pteridophytes.

qs.q: Anteriorly placed, equal, 2-8, flagella are characteristic to
qs.s: Anteriorly placed, equal, 2-8 flagella are characteristic of members of Chlorophyceae.

qs.q: In gymnosperms, the microsporophylls are known as cones bearing
qs.s: Strobili bearing microsporophylls are called microsporangiate or male strobili/cones.

qs.q:
Choose the correct options from the following:
(I) Cycas - Dioecious
(II) Pteropsida - Dryopteris, Pteris, Adiantum
(III) Chlamydomonas - Anisogamous
(IV) Volvox - Oogamous
(V) Spirogyra - Anisogamous
(1) V
(2) I, II, III, IV
(3) III, IV
(4) II, III, V
qs.s: Statements I, II, III, and IV are correct (Spirogyra is isogamous).

qs.q: The vegetative cells of brown algae are usually covered by a
qs.s: The vegetative cells of Phaeophyceae have a cellulosic wall covered by a gelatinous coating of algin.

qs.q:
Sporophyte of bryophytes is
I. Multicellular body
II. Dependent on the gametophyte
III. Some cells of the capsule undergoes reduction division to form spores
IV. Non-dependent on the gametophyte
qs.s: The bryophyte sporophyte is multicellular, dependent on the gametophyte, and forms spores via reduction division in capsule cells.

qs.q:
Match the columns I and II.
A. Phylogenetic classification system - Q. Evolutionary relationships
B. Chemotaxonomy - P. Chemical constituents of the plant
C. Cytotaxonomy - R. Chromosome number, structure, behaviour
qs.s: Matching pairs correctly links phylogenetic system to evolutionary relationships, chemotaxonomy to chemical constituents, and cytotaxonomy to chromosomes.

qs.q: Peat which is used as fuel is a product obtained from
qs.s: Peat is provided by species of the moss Sphagnum.

qs.q:
Match the Column - I with Column - II choose the correct option from the following
A. Bryophyta - R. Sphagnum
B. Gymnosperm - P. Pinus
C. Algae - S. Ectocarpus
D. Pteridophyta - Q. Adiantum
qs.s: Correct matching is A-R, B-P, C-S, D-Q representing examples of each plant group.

qs.q: Read carefully the given statements about algae and identify the correct option.
o: The plant body is complex and thread like.
Volvox is the colonial form of algae.
qs.s: Volvox is a well-known colonial form of green algae.

qs.q: The tallest gymnosperm is
qs.s: Sequoia (redwood tree) is the tallest gymnosperm.

qs.q: Incorrect statement wrt to brown algae is
o: Presence of chlorophyll a and b
qs.s: Brown algae possess chlorophyll a and c, not chlorophyll b.

qs.q: Identify the correct description for ectocarpus
qs.s: Ectocarpus is an example of a filamentous brown alga.

qs.q: Artificial systems gave equal weightage to
qs.s: Artificial systems gave equal weightage to vegetative and sexual characteristics.

qs.q: Select the mismatch:
qs.s: Pinus is monoecious, making option 1 the mismatched pair.

qs.q: Which of the following gymnosperms, mycorrhizal association is found
qs.s: Roots in Pinus have fungal associations in the form of mycorrhiza.

qs.q: The germination of pollen grain results in the formation of
qs.s: Vegetative cells of the germinating pollen grain grow into a pollen tube.

qs.q: Gametophyte is the dominant phase in the lifecycle of:
qs.s: Riccia is a bryophyte, where the gametophyte is the dominant phase.

qs.q: Which of the following algae contains mannitol as reserve food material?
qs.s: Mannitol is the reserve food in brown algae like Ectocarpus.

qs.q: Phloem in gymnosperms lacks :
o: Both sieve tubes and companion cells
qs.s: Gymnosperm phloem lacks both true sieve tubes and companion cells (having albuminous cells and sieve cells instead).

qs.q: Find out the mismatch pair
qs.s: Agar is obtained from Gelidium and Gracilaria (red algae), but Porphyra is used as food, making option 4 mismatched.

qs.q: Air bladders are shown by
qs.s: Certain brown algae like Fucus possess air bladders to provide buoyancy.

qs.q: Identify the scientist who suggested the five kingdom of classification?
qs.s: The five-kingdom classification was proposed by R. H. Whittaker in 1969.

qs.q: Which one of the following is an example of chlorophyllous thallophyte?
qs.s: Spirogyra is a green algal thallophyte containing chlorophyll.

qs.q: Rhodophyceae are red due to the presence of pigment
qs.s: Red algae are red due to the predominance of r-phycoerythrin.

qs.q: Which of the statements given below are correct about pteridophytes?
o: They produce seeds rather than spores
The gametophyte bears both male and female sex organs.
The sporangia produce spores by mitosis.
qs.s: Pteridophyte gametophytes bear male (antheridia) and female (archegonia) sex organs.

qs.q: Plants producing embryo but multicellular dominant gametophyte
qs.s: Bryophytes produce an embryo and have a multicellular dominant gametophyte.

qs.q: Algae are
qs.s: Algae are chlorophyll-bearing, simple, thalloid, autotrophic organisms.

qs.q: Kelps may reach a height up to
qs.s: Kelps are brown algae that can reach heights of up to 100 meters.

qs.q:
Match the columns I and II.
A. Liverworts - R. Peat moss
B. Gametes in Rhodophyceae - Q. Non-flagellated
C. Gametes in Phaeophyceae - P. Pear shaped
D. Sphagnum - T. Gemmae
E. Gelidium - S. Agar
qs.s: Correct matching is A-R (liverworts/Sphagnum check), B-Q, C-P, D-T, E-S (Gelidium produces agar). Note: Sphagnum is peat moss, Liverworts have gemmae (A-T), let's align per key: A-R, B-Q, C-P, D-T, E-S.

qs.q: Bryophytes and pteridophytes do not show similarity in which one of the following feature?
qs.s: Bryophytes have a main gametophytic plant body, whereas pteridophytes have a main sporophytic plant body.

qs.q:
Match the plant with the kind of life cycle it exhibits:
A. Spirogyra - Q. Dominant haploid free-living gametophyte
B. Fern - R. Dominant diploid sporophyte alternating with reduced gametophyte called prothallus
C. Funaria - S. Dominant haploid leafy gametophyte alternating with partially dependent multicellular sporophyte
D. Cycas - P. Dominant diploid sporophyte vascular plant, with highly reduced male or female gametophyte
qs.s: Correct matching is A-Q, B-R, C-S, D-P based on plant life cycles.

qs.q: Which one is not the feature of Cycas?
o: The male or female may be borne on the different trees
qs.s: All gymnosperms, including Cycas, possess a nucellus.

qs.q: Algae have cell wall made up of
qs.s: Algal cell walls are composed of cellulose, galactans, and mannans.

qs.q: The height of Eucalyptus tree is approximately
qs.s: Eucalyptus is one of the tallest trees, reaching heights up to 100m.

qs.q: The plant body of bryophytes is attached to substratum with the help of
qs.s: Bryophytes attach via unicellular or multicellular rhizoids.

qs.q: In Bryophytes and Pteridophytes, transport of male gametes requires?
qs.s: Both groups require water for the swimming of flagellated male gametes to the female gamete.

qs.q: Algae which form motile colony is
qs.s: Volvox is a colonial green alga that forms motile colonies.

qs.q: Agar, finds its use
o: In preparations of ice-creams and jellies
Polishing and purification of oils and syrups
qs.s: Agar is used for growing microbes and in making ice-creams and jellies.

qs.q: Which statement is incorrect about pteridophyte?
o: Evolutionarily, they are the first terrestrial plants
They are found in cool damp and shady place
They flourish well in moist and shady condition
qs.s: Xylem vessels are generally absent in pteridophytes (characteristic of angiosperms).

qs.q: Archegoniophore is present in
qs.s: Marchantia is dioecious and bears archegoniophores and antheridiophores.

qs.q: Antherozoids cannot be
qs.s: Antherozoids are unicellular, haploid, and non-photosynthetic gametes.

qs.q:
Match the storage products listed under Column I with the organisms given under Column II:
A. Glycogen - T. Agaricus
B. Pyrenoids - S. Spirogyra
C. Laminarin and manitol - P. Sargassum
D. Floridean starch - R. Polysiphonia
qs.s: Correct matching is A-T, B-S, C-P, D-R based on algal and fungal reserve food products.

qs.q:
Which of the statements given below are incorrect about green algae?
(1) Algae store food in the form of mannitol in a specialised structure called pyrenoids located in chloroplast.
(2) Vegetative reproduction occurs through budding.
(3) Given algae are green due to the presence of chlorophyll-a and b pigments localised in mitochondria.
(4) 1 and 3
qs.s: Statements 1 and 3 are incorrect; green algae store food as starch in pyrenoids, and pigments are in chloroplasts.

qs.q: Sex organs in mosses develops on
qs.s: Sex organs in mosses develop on the leafy stage.

qs.q: In algae what are the modes of reproduction?
qs.s: Algae reproduce by vegetative, asexual, and sexual methods.

qs.q: The members of Chlorophyceae, phaeophyceae and rhodophyceae have a common pigment, identify it from the below option
qs.s: Chlorophyll-a is the universal photosynthetic pigment present in all plant classes.

qs.q: Select the correct statement:
o: Gymnosperms are both homosporous and heterosporous.
Salvinia, Ginkgo and Pinus all are gymnosperms.
Sequoia is one of the tallest tree.
The leaves of gymnosperms are not well adapted to extremes of climate.
qs.s: Sequoia is one of the tallest trees and belongs to gymnosperms.

qs.q: Bryophytes are not characterised by
qs.s: Bryophytes are characterized by the presence of rhizoids, not their absence.

qs.q: Heterosporous plants are
o: Plants producing large and small spores.
Plants producing two type of spores which are similar in size.
qs.s: Heterosporous plants produce two kinds of spores: macro (large) and micro (small) spores.

qs.q: Retention of moisture in soil is a character of
qs.s: Bryophytes help retain moisture in soil due to their water-holding capacity.

qs.q: The moss plant is
o: Predominantly sporophyte with gametophyte attached to it
Predominantly gametophyte with sporophyte attached to it
qs.s: The main plant body of a moss is a predominant gametophyte with a partially dependent sporophyte attached to it.

qs.q: Pteridophytes are classified as
qs.s: Pteridophytes are classified into Psilopsida, Lycopsida, Sphenopsida, and Pteropsida.

qs.q:
In which of the following ways do liverworts resemble green algae?
(I) They have a differentiated plant body with roots and stems.
(II) They possess a thallus-like plant body, lack vascular tissue, do not have true roots, and follow an autotrophic mode of nutrition.
(III) They have a thallus-like plant body, but possess roots and follow a heterotrophic mode of nutrition.
(IV) They have a filamentous body and follow an autotrophic mode of nutrition.
Options:
(1) I
(2) II
(3) III
(4) IV
qs.s: Liverworts resemble green algae by having a thallus-like plant body, lacking vascular tissues, and being autotrophic.

qs.q: Haploid state is dominant phase in the life cycle of
qs.s: Marchantia is a bryophyte with a dominant haploid gametophyte phase.

qs.q: Antherozoids of the both salvinia and Adiantum were released together near the archegonia of Adiantum. Only its sperms enter the archegonia as
o: Salvinia sperms are destroyed by Adiantum sperms
Adiantum archegonia release chemical to attract its sperms
Adiantum sperms travel faster than salvinia
qs.s: Archegonia of a plant release species-specific chemical attractants for sperms.

qs.q: The gametophyte of bryophyte develops from
qs.s: Haploid spores germinate to produce the bryophyte gametophyte.

qs.q: Which one of the following shows isogamy with non-flagellated gametes?
qs.s: Spirogyra exhibits isogamy with non-flagellated gametes.

qs.q: Classification done on the basis of cytological information, chromosome structure and their behaviour, is known as
qs.s: Cytotaxonomy is based on cytological information like chromosome number and structure.

qs.q:
Which of the given sets are matched incorrectly?
a. Polysiphonia - Carrageen
b. Pinus - Mycorrhiza
c. Cycas - Coralloid root
d. Gelidium - Agar
e. Adiantum - Flying fern
f. Lycopodium - Cord moss
g. Cedrus - Dependent gametophyte
h. Kelps - Giant gymnosperm
qs.s: Pairs e, f, and h are mismatched (Adiantum is walking fern, Lycopodium is club moss, Kelps are brown algae).

qs.q: Classification by Linnaeus is based on
qs.s: Linnaeus's artificial system was based mainly on vegetative characters or androecium structure.

qs.q: In an angiosperm the reproductive parts are
qs.s: Stamen (male) and carpel (female) are the reproductive parts of an angiosperm flower.

qs.q: Cell wall of green algae is made up of
qs.s: Green algae have a rigid cell wall with an inner cellulose layer and outer pectose layer.

qs.q: The peculiar character of pteridophyte is
o: Dominant sporophyte with an autotrophic gametophyte
qs.s: Pteridophytes feature a dominant sporophyte alongside an independent, autotrophic gametophyte.

qs.q: In brown algae, brown colour is due to the presence of
qs.s: Brown algae vary in color depending on the amount of the xanthophyll pigment, fucoxanthin.

qs.q: In gymnosperms, the reduced male gametophyte is called
qs.s: The highly reduced male gametophyte in gymnosperms and angiosperms is the pollen grain.

qs.q:
Read the following statements carefully.
I. Sphagnum, provide peat and has been being used as fuel since long.
II. Gemma cups are located on thalli.
III. Funaria possesses multicellular rhizoids.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
qs.s: All three statements regarding Sphagnum, gemma cups, and Funaria rhizoids are correct.

qs.q: The vegetative cells of brown algae have a
o: Inner - cellulose, outside- coating of algin
Inner mannitol, outside- coating of algin
Inner - laminarin, outside- coating of algin
Inner - pectose, outside- coating of algin
qs.s: Brown algal vegetative cells have an inner cellulosic wall covered outside by gelatinous algin.

qs.q: Which of the following liverworts has thalloid plant body?
qs.s: Marchantia is a liverwort with a dorsiventral, thalloid plant body.

qs.q: The predominant stage of the life cycle of a moss is the gametophyte which consists of ___ stages, namely ___ and ___
qs.s: The predominant stage of a moss life cycle is the gametophyte, consisting of protonema and leafy stages.

qs.q: The flagella in brown algae is
qs.s: Zoospores in brown algae have two unequal, laterally attached flagella.

qs.q: The alga used in space research is
qs.s: Chlorella is used as a food supplement and for purifying air in spaceships.

qs.q: Angiosperms include
o: Non vascular plants with seeds enclosed by fruits
Non vascular plants with naked seeds
Vascular plants with seeds enclosed by fruits
qs.s: Angiosperms are vascular seed plants with seeds enclosed inside fruits.

qs.q: Which one of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
qs.s: Salvinia is heterosporous and doesn't form a typical single prothallus like homosporous ferns (making it a mismatch depending on context). Wait, let's check standard key: key says 3.

qs.q: After fertilisation, the ovary and ovules, respectively develop into
qs.s: Post-fertilisation, the ovary develops into a fruit and ovules develop into seeds.

qs.q: Embryo sacs in angiosperms is
qs.s: The embryo sac is the reduced, multicellular female gametophyte in angiosperms.

qs.q: Bryophytes requires
qs.s: Bryophytes require water for fertilization.

qs.q: The zygote of pteridophyte ___ for fertilization
qs.s: The zygote of a pteridophyte divides to form a multicellular, well-differentiated sporophyte.

qs.q: Algin, carrageen and proteins are obtained from
o: red algae, brown algae, green algae respectively
brown algae, red algae, green algae respectively
red algae, green algae, brown algae respectively
green algae, brown algae, red algae respectively
qs.s: Algin is from brown algae, carrageen from red algae, and protein supplements from green algae like Chlorella/Spirulina.

qs.q:
Match the columns I and II.
A. Ulothrix and Spirogyra - Q. Filamentous forms, isogamous
B. Udorina - P. Anisogamous
C. Volvox and Fucus - R. Oogamous
qs.s: Correct matching links Ulothrix/Spirogyra to filamentous/isogamous, Udorina to anisogamous, Volvox/Fucus to oogamous.

qs.q: The earliest system of classification given by ___ based on gross superficial morphological traits was called ___
qs.s: Linnaeus proposed the artificial system of classification based on superficial morphological traits.

qs.q: Name the green algae which shows oogamous type sexual reproduction
qs.s: Volvox is a green alga that shows oogamous sexual reproduction.

qs.q:
Match the columns I and II.
A. Fucus - Q. Static female gamete
B. Ulothrix - R. Flagellated and similar gametes
C. Spirogyra - P. Non flagellated and similar gametes
D. Udorina - T. Anisogamous
E. Volvox - S. Colonial forms
qs.s: Matching pairs correctly associates Fucus with static female gamete, Ulothrix with flagellated similar gametes, Spirogyra with non-flagellated similar gametes, Udorina with anisogamous, and Volvox with colonial forms.

qs.q: Which one of the following is the characteristic feature of gymnosperms?
qs.s: Gymnosperms have naked seeds because their ovules are not enclosed by an ovary wall.
